text:
carla: Kicking off the phased rollout for release v3.2.1. Plan: US -> EU -> APAC. Change window 22:00-04:00 UTC. Starting with 2% canary in US, 5 minute soak, then 10% -> 25%. Pin EU to v3.2.0 during US ramp.
alice: Copy. Can you confirm capacity headroom for US during the 25% step? Need expected qps and GPU slots.
ben: US warm pool report: baseline 12k qps, warm pool + burst can handle ~4k additional at 95th pct latency target. Thermal cushion ok.
carla: Good. So 25% should be within reserve if routes are split by slice. EU pin stays. APAC won't be touched until both US/EU green.
ellen: Any rollout notes I should add to release notes? Customers get EU pinned behavior callout?
carla: Yes add: "EU pinned to v3.2.0 until US canary validated; APAC staged for next window; no breaking API changes."
deploy-bot: deploy started for v3.2.1 (canary)
```
deploy-bot: action=deploy stage=canary region=us pct=2 version=v3.2.1 id=deploy_2812345678
status=rolling
```
sre-oncall: Quick check, what's the rollback signal? CPU > 85% + p99 latency regression > 200ms over baseline for 3 consecutive minutes?
carla: Yes. Rollback triggers: p99 increase >200ms OR error rate >0.5% sustained >5m OR OOM events. Notify #incidents and execute immediate pin to v3.2.0.
alice: Got it. I'll watch the dashboards. I'll also run the synthetic prompts against the canary to validate quality regression set.
ben: Implementing traffic slice pin rules now. If we need a fast rollback we can flip the slice routing to pinned version in ~30s.
ellen: Add customer-impact note: "If rollback occurs EU will remain on v3.2.0; customers in US may see transient failures while we revert."
carla: Can we get a capacity smoke test at 10% before doing 25%?
ben: Yes I'll bump to 10% after 5m soak and run smoke at 80% of expected load.
deploy-bot: canary health check (5m): ok. p50/p95/p99 within baseline thresholds.
carla: @sre-oncall please stand by for potential rollback window 22:20-22:30 UTC based on US behavior.
sre-oncall: Standing by. Will escalate to on-call sig if thresholds breach.
alice: Synthetic eval reports: no regression on prompts set A, slight paraphrase variance on set B but within tolerance.
carla: Proceed to 10% then run smoke. If smoke passes, proceed to 25% and hold for 10m. If anything odd, trigger rollback and pin.
ben: 10% traffic applied -> warm cache filling. Smoke run in progress.

```
Smoke result: requests=12000, errors=0.08%, p99=320ms (baseline 300ms) -> within tolerance (threshold 350ms)
```
carla: Looks good. Moving to 25%.
deploy-bot: action=deploy stage=canary region=us pct=25 version=v3.2.1 id=deploy_2812345678_step2
status=rolling

ben: Monitoring CPU/GPU temps and queue length. Warm pool holding.
sre-oncall: No alerts. Latency stable.
alice: Running second round of synthetics across edge nodes.
ellen: Draft release note update sent to #release-notes for review.
carla: If all stays green for 10m we consider US canary successful and start EU unpin decision meeting.
ben: EU pin remains until we get green in US. If US rollback -> we keep EU pinned and cancel APAC.
carla: Agreed. Also if we see regional memory pressure, we'll enable quantized fallback for that slice only.
alice: Noted. I'll prepare canary logs + eval artifact for the postmortem in case we need it.
deploy-bot: canary health check (10m at 25%): ok. p99 310ms, errors 0.09%
carla: US canary declared healthy. Scheduling EU pin review in 15m. APAC freeze remains.
sre-oncall: Good job team :thumbsup:
ellen: Updating release notes to reflect phased success and EU unpin pending review.
carla: Thanks all. After the EU review, we'll do a short post-canary notes and a final rollout plan for APAC in the next change window.
alice: One last thing — please ensure runbook step 4 has the exact commands to flip slice pin immediately (we tested offline but add command snippet).
ben: Adding snippet to runbook now:
```
# Flip routing to pinned version
redwoodctl route set --slice europe --version v3.2.0 --force
```
carla: Perfect. Closing thread for now, will re-open if EU review surfaces issues. :rocket:
